title: D NDE 7394
content: This memory or 'experience' remains unchanged in my memory since those years. At the time, I was a regular customer of the municipal outside swimming pool. I went there all summer days with 5 or 6 friends. We passed our time by playing and horsing around in the water. As an excellent swimmer and diver, I was jumping up and down on the 3-meter fiberglass diving board. On the moment to take off, I made a wrong movement and landed on the water, making an enormous 'flat landing' on my belly and chest. The shock was very violent, which cut my respiration completely. I couldn't breathe as I got out of the water grabbing the rim. I was crawling towards my friends whom were laughing and making fun of me. It was at this moment that I realized, I was seeing from another angle; I could watch myself on the ground while I was floating above my body. I didn't feel pain anymore. I floated in the wind going faster and higher. I didn't know if this would be stopping or if I would continue to go higher up into the sky. I saw the place globally, looking at the swimming pool, public gardens, the stadium, streets, roofs of the houses, at an angle that is just impossible to describe. I saw the alarm of people on the ground while I floating above them. I remember that I saw that I was wearing a red swimsuit that summer. A feeling of well-being came over me. I had no notion at all of time passing anymore. It is so impossible to say if it took 1 minute or 5. Then in a split second, I was caught and sucked towards my body. Air could again enter my lungs. As I came back to consciousness, the pain came back. I was back to dry land, which marked the end of the 'experience'. I immediately told my friends what happened; they continued to laugh while saying, 'What nonsense!'

context.nde_cause_other_detail: Impact from a wrong takeoff on a 3-meter diving board causing a violent flat landing on belly/chest and complete cessation of breathing.

stage_sequence.sequence_variation_description: OBE with aerial viewing of the area, then sudden involuntary return ('caught and sucked towards my body'). No tunnel, beings, or life review described.

unique_elements.nonstandard_elements: Aerial/overhead viewing of the swimming pool area and surroundings (gardens, stadium, streets, roofs) after breath was cut off from impact; sudden 'sucked' return coinciding with air re-entering lungs and pain returning.
unique_elements.notable_quotes:
“I realized, I was seeing from another angle; I could watch myself on the ground while I was floating above my body.”
“Then in a split second, I was caught and sucked towards my body. Air could again enter my lungs.”
